When a hook throws an error during `cleanup` we want to run all the other cleanups so we can avoid memory leaks and end in a consistent UI.

For this we'll need to always clear the `hook._cleanup` function so that we don't call it twice. During unmount we want to *ensure* we run through all hooks and even if we error we defer that to only bubble up the latest error.

Fix implemented in `hooks/src/index.js` (the hook coordinator), mirroring the upstream resolution of preactjs/preact#3329/#3345:

1. **`HookCoordinator.invokeCleanup`** (hooks/src/index.js:364) — clears `hook._cleanup` *before* invoking it, so a cleanup that throws is never invoked a second time (e.g. once when the pending effect is flushed, and again during unmount, which previously re-threw `oops` uncaught).
2. **`HookCoordinator.unmount`** (hooks/src/index.js:148) — runs the cleanup of *every* hook even when one throws (per-hook try/catch, keeping the latest error), and only afterwards forwards that error to `options._catchError`. This ensures unmount completes — remaining cleanups run and the DOM is fully removed — before the error reaches the boundary.
